 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellants/claimants under Section 173 (1) of the Indian Motor Vehicles Act challenging the judgment and award dated 01.04.2022 passed in MVC No.102/2019 by the Court of VIII Additional Small Causes Judge and the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (SCCH-5) at Bengaluru (for short hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal') fixing the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (SCCH-5) at Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel on both the sides.
3. The ranks of the parties before the Tribunal is retained for the sake of convenience.

4. The case of the claimants are that they have filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the M.V.
Act, 1989 for claiming compensation from the respondents in respect of death of the deceased Kheman Naiya, who died in the road traffic accident dated 29.07.2018.

It is alleged that when the deceased was crossing the road near Neraloor Bus Stop, NH-7 Road,
Hosur- Bengaluru Road, Attibele Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru a Tata Indica Car bearing registration No.KA-34-M-5478 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased.
Due to which, deceased fell down and sustained blood stained injuries, he was taken to the hospital but deceased died in the hospital during the treatment.
Accordingly, the claim petition was filed.

6. The respondent-insurer has filed statement of objection by denying the accident, age, occupation and also taken contention that the vehicle was not driven in high speed the deceased has negligently crossed the road without following the traffic discipline and therefore he himself contributed for the accident.
Hence, prayed for dismissing the claim petition.
7. On the basis of the pleadings, tribunal has framed following issues NC: 2024:KHC:27649 1.

Whether petitioners prove that, deceased Sri.Kheman Naiya, S/o Sahdev Naiya, aged about 43 years, who died in a road traffic accident that occurred on 29.07.2018 at about 9.00 p.m. while deceased was crossing the road near Neraloor Bus Stop, NH-7 Road, Bengaluru-Hosur Road,
Attibele, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru, at that time, a driver of the Tata Indica Car bearing registration No.KA-34- M-5478 driven in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased, as a result of which, he fell down and sustained fatal injuries and died, as mentioned in the claim petition?
2. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
if so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

The respondents have not lead any evidence nor got marked any documents.

9. After hearing the arguments, Tribunal has answered issue Nos.1 and 2 partly in the affirmative and allowed the petition in-part by awarding compensation of NC: 2024:KHC:27649 Rs.17,41,686/-
by taking Rs.12,500/- per month as notional income for the accident occurred in the year 2018.

25%
is added towards future prospects and 1/5th of the total income has been deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased as there are more than 5 dependents and awarded Rs.2,80,000/- towards the consortium for all 7 persons (40,000 x 7) and conventional amount with additional 10% as per the Pranay Sethi & Ors. case and accordingly Rs.20,68,123/- as under:-

However the Tribunal while answering issue No.1 has contended that there was a contributory negligence on the part of the deceased, who negligently crossed the road by coming suddenly to the middle of the road as per Ex.P.7.
Hence, the Tribunal has attributed 30% of negligence on the part of the deceased and 70% of negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, which is under challenge.
11. The learned counsel for the appellant has contended that there is no evidence lead by the respondent, no driver has been examined by the respondent.
Such being the case, question of contributory negligence does not arise.
Hence, prayed for setting aside the finding of contributory negligence.

12. Per contra, respondent's counsel has contended that document at Ex.P.7 produced by the claimants themselves reveals that accident has occurred in the middle of the road, where the deceased was crossing the NC: 2024:KHC:27649 high way without following traffic discipline where Muniya Devi vs The United India Insurance Company Ltd on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4590552/
4 there is no pedestrian/zebra cross at the spot.

sentences.text: Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly considered 30% of the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
Hence, prays for dismissing the appeal.
13. In support of his contention he has relied upon the judgment of Supreme Court reported in 2007 AIR SCW 3591 in the case of Oriental Insurance Company Limited -VS- Premlata Shukla and Ors.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Limited -VS- Premlata Shukla and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. After hearing the arguments, perused the records the point that arise for consideration is:-

Whether the Tribunal has justified in giving finding in issue No.1 that the accident was occurred due to the contributory negligence of the deceased as well as driver of the Car, which calls for interference?
15. On perusal of record, the accident and death of the deceased is not in dispute only the contributory negligence were in dispute.
At most the police have filed NC: 2024:KHC:27649 the charge sheet against the driver of the car for causing the accident.
The driver of the car has not challenged the charge sheet or not lead any evidence before the Court.
Even the insurer has not chosen to bring the driver of the car for producing any evidence to show that there was a contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.

16. However, in view of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Premlata Shukla and Ors stated supra case, when the document produced by the claimants themselves is an admitted document and there is no ground to discard the same.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Premlata Shukla and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Tribunal by considering document at Ex.P.7 - Sketch prepared by the police at the accident spot clearly reveals that the accident had occurred on the middle of the road, which is NH-7,
Bengaluru-Hosur Road.
Therefore, the Tribunal has considered that there is contributory negligence on the part of the deceased himself.

The document of the claimants reveals that the deceased was crossing the highway and the accident had occurred in the middle of the highway, which reveals that deceased without observing the passing vehicles on the high way and in a speed he has entered the high way in the middle of the road, where he has sustained injury and succumbed to the same.
Therefore, it cannot be said that there is no negligence on the part of the deceased.
18. It is not the case of the claimants that there was a zebra/pedestrian cross, where the deceased had crossed the high way.
Such being the case, definitely there is contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
However, the document reveals that the accident was occurred near the bus stop.
Such being the case, I am of the view instead of taking 30% negligence, I propose to consider only 10% towards the negligence of the deceased for the contribution in the accident.

sentences.text: Accordingly, I hold that the Tribunal has rightly considered the contributory negligence on the part of the - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:27649 deceased as well as offending vehicle.
However the percentage of contribution attributed on the deceased i.e., 30% is high and hence, the same is reduced to 10%.

Accordingly, I pass the following:-
ORDER 1.
The appeal is allowed in-part.
2. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal of Rs.17,41,686/- is hereby confirmed and the contributory negligence is reduced to 10% from 30% attributed by the Tribunal.
3. The remaining appropriation made by the Tribunal is hereby confirmed.
